claims.text: RFC 9457: the type member is a JSON string containing a URI reference that identifies the problem type; consumers MUST use the type URI (after resolution, if necessary) as the problem type's primary identifier.
RFC 9457: the title member is advisory, a short human-readable summary of the problem type, included for users who cannot discover the semantics of the type URI.
RFC 9457: the detail member is specific to the occurrence, and consumers SHOULD NOT parse it for information; extensions are the more suitable way to obtain such information.
RFC 9457: when the type member is not present, its value is assumed to be "about:blank"; about:blank as a problem type means the problem has no additional semantics beyond the HTTP status code.

RFC 9457: problem type definitions may extend the problem details object with additional members (extensions); clients consuming problem details MUST ignore any such extensions that they don't recognize.
Order.Cancel() throws OrderStatusException with code "already-cancelled" when Status is "cancelled" and code "already-shipped" when Status is "shipped"; the third argument is the message.

ExceptionHandlingMiddleware answers every OrderStatusException with 409, title "Order status does not allow this", detail = ex.Message, type = ProblemTypeBase + ex.Code, and the orderId extension; ProblemTypeBase is "https://donhang.local/problems/".

PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel calls OrderService.CancelOrderAsync, which calls order.Cancel(); at stage-2 cancelling an order whose status is already cancelled, or is shipped, answers 409 through the middleware.

In ExceptionHandlingMiddleware, the KeyNotFoundException (404) and ArgumentException (400) branches call WriteProblemAsync without a type, so Type stays null; WriteProblemAsync writes ex.Message as Detail.

ASP.NET Core 10: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ProblemDetails marks Type (and the other standard members) to be ignored when null during JSON serialization, so a null Type is omitted from the body; Extensions entries are written as top-level members.

claims.text: Order.Ship() on an order with status "new" passes the cancelled and shipped checks and throws OrderStatusException with code "not-paid", giving type https://donhang.local/problems/not-paid; OrdersApiTests.ShipOrder_StaffAndNewOrder_Returns409NotPaid asserts this value.
DonHang.App's ApiProblem.fromResponse reads a missing type as 'about:blank'.
RFC 9110: 409 Conflict means the request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the target resource.
A client should branch on type rather than on status code alone when one status code can carry several problem types, because the status names only the class of failure.
RFC 9457: the standard members of a problem details object are type, status, title, detail and instance; consumers SHOULD NOT automatically dereference the type URI.
